content: Petroleum products are valuable materials derived from crude oil, also known as petroleum, through processing in oil refineries. The composition of crude oil and market demand determine the proportions of various petroleum products that refineries produce. The majority of these products serve as energy carriers, such as different grades of fuel oil and gasoline. Additionally, refineries produce other chemicals, some of which are utilized in chemical processes to manufacture plastics and other useful materials. Crude oil typically contains a small percentage of sulfur, and as a result, significant quantities of sulfur are often produced as a byproduct during refining. Other byproducts include hydrogen and carbon in the form of petroleum coke. The hydrogen generated is frequently used as an intermediate product in other refinery processes, such as hydrocracking (hydrogen catalytic cracking) and hydrodesulfurization. Major Products of Oil Refineries Oil refineries perform various operations, including blending different feedstocks, adding appropriate additives, providing short-term storage, and preparing products for bulk transportation via trucks, barges, product ships, and railcars. Gaseous Fuels: Products like propane are stored and transported in liquid form under pressure in specialized railcars to distributors. Liquid Fuels: These include automotive and aviation-grade gasoline, kerosene, various aviation turbine fuels, and diesel fuels. Additives such as dyes, detergents, anti-knock agents, oxygenates, and anti-fungal compounds are incorporated as needed. These fuels are shipped by barge, rail, and tanker ships. In some cases, they are transported regionally through dedicated pipelines to end consumers, such as aviation jet fuel to major airports, or through multi-product pipelines using separators called pipeline inspection gauges (pigs). Lubricants: These include light machine oils, motor oils, and greases, which may have viscosity stabilizers added as required. They are typically shipped in bulk to offsite packaging plants. Wax (Paraffin): This is used in applications such as packaging frozen foods. It is often shipped in bulk to facilities where it is prepared as packaged blocks. Sulfur and Sulfuric Acid: These are byproducts of sulfur removal from petroleum, which may contain up to a few percent sulfur in the form of organic sulfur compounds. Sulfur and sulfuric acid are valuable industrial materials. Sulfuric acid is often prepared and shipped as its precursor, oleum. Bulk Tar: This is shipped for offsite packaging and used in applications such as tar-and-gravel roofing. Asphalt: Asphalt is used as a binder for gravel to create asphalt concrete, which is employed in paving roads, parking lots, and similar surfaces. An asphalt unit prepares bulk asphalt for shipment. Petroleum Coke: This is used in specialty carbon products, such as certain types of electrodes, or as a solid fuel. Petrochemicals and Petrochemical Feedstocks: These are often sent to petrochemical plants for further processing. Petrochemicals may include olefins or their precursors, as well as various types of aromatic petrochemicals.
